takeaway: An LLM Actor retries a task over trials; after each failed trial a Self-Reflection LLM turns the trajectory and its sparse reward into a verbal lesson stored in long-term memory, which conditions the next trial.
problem: Scalar rewards are too sparse for an LLM agent to learn from across trials without weight updates.

contributions.name: Self-Reflection
contributions.solves: turns a sparse reward into informative verbal feedback (verbal reinforcement)
contributions.shown_by: orange accent box on the return path, its output sr_t on an orange arrow into memory, and a real reflection text in the example

contributions.name: Long-term memory (mem)
contributions.solves: carries lessons over trials as context for the Actor, bounded by Ω
contributions.shown_by: orange store left of the Actor feeding it 'mem'; the Actor box names its short-term memory (trajectory)

mechanism.explains: one trial: Actor acts in the environment (a_t, o_t), the Evaluator scores τ_t (r_t = M_e(τ_t)), Self-Reflection writes sr_t into mem, the next trial reads mem — until the Evaluator deems τ_t correct
